\section{The opening and the compilation: disagreements between the sources}\label{sec:gen-opening-disagreements}

\begin{sloppypar}
Short forms in this section. Specification files are under \file{doc/leanvm/body/}: \code{08:} is
\file{08-end-to-end-protocol.tex}, \code{B:} is \file{b-polynomial-commitment-scheme.tex}. Rust
files: \code{whir.rs}, \code{whir_config.rs} are under \file{crates/pcs/src/}; \code{fs/} is
\file{crates/fiat_shamir/src/}; \code{mod.rs} is \file{crates/lean_vm/src/cpu/mod.rs}. \code{py:}
is \file{python-verifier/verifier.py}. These are at leanVM's pin \code{a386121f}. \code{bp:} is the
blueprint at leanerVM \code{b435631}. The number after the colon is the line.
\end{sloppypar}

The three sources agree on the pool, the batching challenge, the power of each claim and the
batched target and weight (\cref{tab:gen-opening-lambda}); there is no sumcheck between $λ$ and
WHIR in any of them (\cref{sec:gen-opening-after-lambda}). The two verifiers agree with each other
on WHIR message for message, the Python being a transcription of the Rust
(\cref{sec:gen-opening-whir}), and on the chain row by row (\cref{tab:gen-opening-chain}); their
one divergence is in the proof format they read (item 4). The specification is silent on the
Fiat--Shamir chain, the rate and several checks; and the deployed WHIR schedule differs from the
specification's Protocol B.6 in four ways (items 6 to 9), none of which the blueprint records
(\cref{f:opening-whir-facts}).

\multicolumn{4}{@{}l}{\textit{Between the three sources}} \\
\midrule
1 & The Fiat--Shamir chain and the proof object
  & §8.4 of the specification is \code{TODO} (\code{08:44-46}); §8.5's ``Setup'' says only that the
  initial state is ``seeded by the public input, the bytecode and Flock's BLAKE2s R1CS matrices''
  (\code{08:55}). The Rust is the only source; the Python transcribes it and agrees on every row of
  \cref{tab:gen-opening-chain}.
  & states the tags, the seed and the squeeze correctly (\code{bp:325}); invites the other reading
  of the step (\cref{f:opening-chain-step}) \\
2 & The rate
  & The specification names no rate (\code{08:55}); both verifiers read the announced rate and
  reject it outside $[1, 4]$ (\code{mod.rs:167}, \code{py:1377}; S-rate of
  \cref{tab:gen-opening-checks}).
  & \lean{Sizes.Admissible} lacks the rate window (\cref{f:bus-admissible}) \\
3 & The closing list of the specification (\code{08:100})
  & ``the caps'' omits the rate window and the stacking window; ``every sumcheck's rounds'' is not a
  check in either verifier (W1); ``the PCS opening'' stands for M1 to M7 and W2 to W5, and grinding
  (G1, G2) is absent from Annex B altogether. The canonical encodings (B2, B3, B10 of
  \cref{tab:gen-bus-checks}; R2), full consumption (R4) and grinding are in both verifiers and not
  in the specification.
  & \lean{verify} inherits these omissions unless Layer 12 lists the checks
  (\cref{sec:gen-opening-checks}) \\
4 & The proof format, and the Python's level-0 leaves
  & The Rust prover emits the pruned wire form; the Rust verifier emits the raw form after
  accepting; the Python reads the raw form (\code{fs/transcript.rs:9-19, 138-143, 198-203};
  \code{py:322-330}). In the raw form the level-0 leaf carries the full 64-word image and the
  Python does not check that the absent lanes are zero (\code{py:1049}): run standalone on an
  adversarial raw proof it accepts a commitment whose absent lanes are nonzero (the citation check
  agrees by reading; the Python was not run on such a proof), while the Rust
  verifier supplies the zero prefix itself (\code{fs/merkle.rs:53-58}): the Python's accepted set
  is strictly larger than the Rust's on this point. Soundness-neutral (M2 of
  \cref{tab:gen-opening-checks}); a divergence in accepted sets nonetheless.
  & unspecified: \lean{merkleVerify} has the raw shape, the fixture is the prover's pruned form
  (\cref{f:opening-merkle-format}) \\
5 & A stale comment in the Rust
  & \code{whir.rs:393-395} says ``one Merkle leaf of \code{num_interleaved * 16} bytes''; the code
  hashes $24·\mathit{num\_interleaved}$ bytes (\code{whir.rs:463}). The citation check found more
  at the pin: \code{whir.rs:1364-1365} says level 0 grinds ``0 bits in the production profile''
  (and \code{whir.rs:1771-1772} in the test-only dense verifier), while every level grinds 17 bits
  (\code{whir_config.rs:922, 955, 988}, asserted at \code{whir_config.rs:1027} and
  \code{whir.rs:2485}); \code{whir.rs:1239-1241} and \code{1636-1637} mention fold grinds, and the
  pinned code has none.
  & --- (for \file{docs/leanvm-target.md}, \cref{f:opening-stale-leaf-comment}) \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{4}{@{}l}{\textit{The deployed WHIR schedule against the specification's Protocol B.6 (\code{B:100-123})}} \\
\midrule
6 & Per-claim intro messages before the batching challenge
  & The specification sends, after $λ_i$, one round polynomial $h_1$ of the batched claim
  (\code{B:111}). The Rust sends a round polynomial \emph{per claim} (the residual's, which is the
  last fold message; the OOD claim's, \code{whir.rs:1206}, before $λ_i$ is drawn; the query batch's,
  \code{whir.rs:1406}, after it), and both sides form the batched $h_1$ by linearity
  (\code{RoundQuad::fold}, \code{whir.rs:548-554}). Equivalent claims, more prover messages.
  Soundness-neutral; transcript-relevant. (The citation check corrected the dossier, which had all
  the intro messages ``before or after'' $λ_i$ and ``two verifier challenges in a row ($λ_i$ then
  $r_1$) with no prover message between them'': the query batch's intro follows $λ_i$, prover
  \code{whir.rs:1373} then \code{1405-1406}, verifier \code{2123} then \code{2142}, \code{py:1044}
  then \code{1057}, and its claim depends on $λ_i$, whose powers weight the queries,
  \code{whir.rs:1374}; the challenges that follow one another with no prover message between are the
  query positions and $λ_i$, \code{whir.rs:1370} then \code{1373}, \code{2122} then \code{2123},
  \code{py:1041} then \code{1044}.)
  & not recorded; \lean{whirOpen} is ``stated exactly as Protocol B.1'' (\code{bp:1185}) \\
7 & Grinding
  & 17 bits at every level, including the last, ground after the level's root (or
  $f_{\mathrm{final}}$) and before its positions (\code{whir_config.rs:57-60, 335-336}); \code{bits = 0}
  would still read a canonical zero nonce (\code{fs/lib.rs:165-174}). Not in Annex B (the status
  file records it, its finding S12).
  & not recorded in Layer 11; Layer 12's \lean{grind} (\cref{tab:gen-opening-layer12}) \\
8 & The lane relayout
  & Level 0 folds the stack's \emph{top} six coordinates (the lane index), the later levels the low
  coordinates of the current fold; the verifier rotates the terminal point left by 6 before
  evaluating $\mle{W}_λ$ (\code{whir.rs:2297-2306}, \code{py:1079}). Annex B states it only in
  ``Optimizations'' (\code{B:380}).
  & nowhere mentioned; a \lean{verify} without it evaluates $\mle{W}_λ$ at the wrong point and
  rejects every Rust proof \\
9 & The last round message
  & Omitted (\code{whir.rs:1471-1475}, \code{:2256-2261}; \code{py:1073-1074}): the verifier's last
  running claim is checked directly against $\mle{f}_{\mathrm{final}}$, so the message that would
  carry it is redundant. The specification says nothing about the last message (\code{B:120}).
  & not recorded \\
\end{longtable}

The OOD count agrees: one per level $≥ 1$ and none at level 0 (\code{whir_config.rs:677-684},
\code{:829-841}; \code{whir.rs:1261-1265} ``L0 takes no OOD sample''), as Annex B (\code{B:105}
``No OOD sample is taken'') and the blueprint (\code{bp:1186-1187}) say.
